# Genesis Apocryphon Column 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 5 | **Condition:** Fragmentary

---

**5:1** [...] Then Enoch answered and said to Methuselah his son [...]

**5:2** [...] go, say to Lamech your son [...]

**5:3** [...] the child is truly his and from his seed [...]

**5:4** [...] and not from the Watchers [...] and not from the sons-of-heaven [...]

**5:5** [...] this-one [...] is truthfully his [...]

**5:6** [...] and his name shall-be-called Noah [...]

**5:7** [...] and he will-be for you the righteous-one [...]

**5:8** [...] a rest and a repose [...] for him and for his sons [...]

**5:9** [...] for all the generations of-eternity [...]

**5:10** [...] and there-will-be a great destruction on the earth [...]

**5:11** [...] a flood [...] and great destruction for one year [...]

**5:12** [...] and he alone will-survive [...] and his sons [...]

**5:13** [...] and all the earth will-be-corrupted [...]

**5:14** [...] the wickedness [...] and the violence [...]

**5:15** [...] and he-will-be [...] the righteous-one [...] the perfect-one [...]

**5:16** [...]

**5:17** [...]

**5:18** [...]

**5:19** [...]

**5:20** [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 5 preserves Enoch's prophetic answer. He confirms Noah's legitimate paternity and prophesies both the coming flood and Noah's survival. "Rest and repose" (nuach ve-niyach) is a wordplay on the name Noah (Noach), echoing Genesis 5:29. "The righteous one, the perfect one" (tsaddiq, tamim) mirrors Genesis 6:9.*
